_comment: THE CLOSED SET of reasons the chain-ingestion pipeline may give for not tracing a
THIS FILE IS DATA BECAUSE TWO LANGUAGES NEED IT. `tools/chain/lib/refusal.mjs` is the
producer side and `src/blocktracer/chain/refusal_reasons.nim` is the publisher side, and
a set that is closed in one and open in the other is not closed. The Nim side reads this
file with `staticRead` at compile time, so a member added here is a member there without
anyone remembering to copy it, and a member REMOVED here breaks the Nim build rather
than silently letting a stale id through the validator.
The reasoning behind each member, the conditions that map onto it and the runtime error
classes that reach it are in `tools/chain/lib/refusal.mjs`. This file carries only what
`absent` MAY NEVER BE A MEMBER. Trace-Artifacts.md §6 reserves it for an execution the
chain never published — the Aztec private half — which is a statement about the chain.
Every member here is a statement about US.
`durability` is load-bearing, not decoration: `tools/capture/expectations.mjs` grades a
transaction page on whether its durability claim is supported by the cause it printed.
permanent   nothing this pipeline can do will produce a trace for this transaction
repairable  a better runtime, a mirrored corpus or a longer budget would trace it

reasons.condition: The transaction is not at index 0 of its block. The historical-state mechanism answers reads at the settling block's PARENT, and that is the state only the first transaction saw; transaction k>0 saw the parent state plus the effects of the k before it, and no node method serves that intermediate view — it exists only inside the sequencer. Replaying against the parent anyway would read every slot an earlier transaction touched at a stale value, fail nothing, and produce a confidently wrong trace.

The node no longer serves the transaction's body and the file store cannot supply it either. getTxByHash reads the mempool, which is emptied at finalization; getTxEffect reads the archive, which is not — so the effects remain visible after the body is gone, which is why such a transaction is in the snapshot at all.

reasons.statedBy: tools/chain/backfill-bodies.mjs classify, outcome `unavailable`; routed by tools/chain/ingest-range.mjs replayRange
reasons.condition: The source that serves transaction bodies COULD NOT BE ASKED about this key — a 5xx, a 429, a TLS failure, a transport error or a timeout. Nothing is known about whether the body exists, so this is a statement about the run and not about the corpus, and it is separate from body-unavailable for exactly the reason backfill-bodies.mjs keeps `unavailable` apart from `absent`: a 404 is the store saying it does not hold the key, and a 503 is the store saying nothing at all. Folding the second into the first published "this transaction can never be re-executed" — durability permanent — off the back of somebody else's outage. It is also separate from not-attempted, whose every narrative asserts the body IS obtainable from the file store: that claim is precisely what a run that could not reach the store has failed to establish, and re-publishing it would be asserting the thing that just could not be checked. Aztec bodies have a single source with no failover (Chain-Data-Ingestion.md §4.8), so this member's count is the measure of how much of a range is outstanding for want of that one host.
A contract the transaction executed has no artifact provable against its class's artifactHash, so the execution cannot be resolved to the code that produced it.

The state the replay must read cannot be obtained at the depth it is required at: the settling block, or the parent it reads through, is not served. Distinct from body-unavailable, which is about the transaction; this is about the STATE.

reasons.statedBy: tools/chain/lib/replay.mjs refusalName, from the driver's stderr
reasons.condition: The replay runtime declined by name for a condition none of the four above describes. The runtime defines error classes by the dozen and gains more, so this member exists to keep OUR set closed while THEIRS is open — the class name travels beside it in `refusal` and its message in `detail`, so the specific condition is always recoverable from the row.
The driver reported a completed execution and wrote no container, so there is nothing to step. Publishing a row that points at a missing container would be worse than saying so.

Nothing about this transaction or about the chain stopped it being traced — THE RUN STOPPED. Three producers reach this member and all three are statements about the run: a live capture that was inside the window with the body still served and reached its own --max first; a historic range ingested without --replay, whose body the keyless TxFileStore does hold and which this run simply did not fetch; and a run whose endpoint began rate-limiting it, which says nothing whatever about the height it was asking about. It is separate for the same reason backfill-bodies.mjs keeps `unavailable` apart from `absent`: a budget, a flag or somebody else's rate limit must never be able to masquerade as a property of the chain.
